learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.evidence: Selected only salt: same10% price rise with1% salt purchase decline and20% ticket decline.
Set price rise10: salt sales−1%, revenue+8.9%; switched tickets at10: sales−20%, revenue−12%. Show why required both comparisons.
Read1.1×0.99=1.089 and1.1×0.8=.88, taller versus narrower revenue box, elasticity label and invented-reactions/one-step/revenue-not-profit limitation.
Actual dark1257x936 screenshots showed green salt rectangle larger than dashed original, red ticket rectangle narrower, and readable reveal after scrolling.

prediction.reason: Same price change with different buyer reactions makes a useful commitment.

interaction.reason: Two products preserve the price step while changing response.

payoff.reason: Arithmetic and rectangle changes explain the opposite outcomes.
payoff.evidence: 1.1×.99 and1.1×.8 tied to height and width.

clarity.reason: Familiar sales example and explicit model limits.
clarity.evidence: Invented buyers; revenue not profit repeated.

transfer.reason: Names the general mechanism but provides no new application exercise.
transfer.evidence: Price elasticity defined after the same comparison.

surprise.reason: Higher price can reduce revenue despite the same increase.

visualExplanation.reason: Rectangle area encodes the product and retains comparison outline.
visualExplanation.evidence: Taller narrower ticket box versus dashed baseline.

practicalValue.reason: Separates revenue from price and profit in an everyday decision.
practicalValue.evidence: Buyer response and model limits explicit.

depth.reason: One price step shows one relationship with limitations.
depth.evidence: No cost model or new case.
